title: Attestation Object (ZIFFER-SPEC-001 §8.6, AT-1 / AT-8 / AT-8a / AT-8b / AT-9)
description:
A signed human act bound to a `proposal_hash`. Carried on leg F4.4 of the leg register (ZIFFER-DEPLOY-001 Annex A). F4.3 named the signing act inside the approval domain, which crosses no domain boundary and is therefore not a leg (DP-83); ACP-86 retired the id rather than reusing it, and AT-1 and AT-8a are cited on F4.4, where the object arrives.

WHY THIS SCHEMA IS CLOSED, AND WHY THAT IS THE SECURITY PROPERTY RATHER THAN A STYLE CHOICE. AT-8b: every AT-1 field is REQUIRED; there are no optional fields, no defaultable fields, and no extension points. An object carrying an unknown field, or omitting any AT-1 field, MUST be rejected — never normalized, never defaulted. That is why `additionalProperties` is false and why `required` lists every property, and it is the one place in this repository where an absent-value rule would be a DEFECT rather than a control: `x-acp-absent` deliberately appears nowhere below.

The reason is Z4. AT-8a pinned the canonicalizer but not the field set. Given ANY optional field, an object present-as-null and the same object with the field omitted are EACH valid canonical CBOR, hash to TWO DISTINCT ids, and therefore claim TWO ledger slots — one attestation, consumed twice. T-14 attestation amplification reopens through the very mechanism Y1b closed. Canonicalization cannot fix it: the ambiguity is in the field set, not the encoding. Mechanized as `Z4_OptionalFieldYieldsTwoIds`.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANYONE EDITING THIS FILE: adding a field here is a BREAKING change requiring a `receipt_version` increment, never an additive one (AT-8b). A future revision that adds an optional field to be helpful reopens T-14.

ENCODING. The wire form is canonical CBOR, RFC 8949 §4.2 (AT-8a) — the same canonicalization as the receipt (WE-1/WE-2). JCS (RFC 8785) MUST NOT be used for this object; JCS is the Proposal's rule and mixing them is the encoding split at the point it does the most damage. JSON here is the diagnostic form the schema is written against, never an accepted input. An object whose RECEIVED encoding is not the canonical one MUST be rejected and MUST NOT be re-serialized and accepted.

WHAT IS NOT A FIELD. `attestation_id` is DERIVED, not carried: it is SHA-256 over the canonical CBOR encoding of this object (AT-1, AT-8a) and the Executor recomputes it (§9.3 step 7b(v)). Transmitting it for trust is what v1.3.2 did, and under one compromised KMS a receipt bearing a genuine quorum raised for proposal P1 verified against an attacker-chosen P2 — Y1. A schema that gave `attestation_id` a property would invite exactly that read, so it has none.

SUITE 12 CLASSIFICATION. Every field below is class T at the schema layer — this document constrains SHAPE, and shape is not authority. The Executor's obligations are elsewhere and are not restated here (DP-3/DP-84): `proposal_hash` is bound (9.3-3), floor-only risk is RECOMPUTED and never read from here (TR-8), and `required_count` is subject to AT-9's two disjoint rules described on that property.

alg.description:
The suite this attestation was raised under. CR-1: every signed structure carries an explicit `alg` naming a suite registered in the signed bundle, and an unregistered or unknown name fails closed rather than being resolved to a known one.

IT IS AN AT-1 FIELD, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT BESIDE THE SIGNATURE. CR-5 makes `alg` signature-covered, so it sits inside the canonical CBOR whose SHA-256 is `attestation_id` (AT-8a). An issuer who could relabel the suite without changing the object would hand a verifier a hybrid entry to check as a classical one, and CR-3's conjunctive rule would be decorative at the point it is applied. PB-8 records the same reasoning for the bundle signature file and anchor.schema.json restates it for the anchor; this is the third artifact it governs and the one where the field set is closed by AT-8b, so a verifier reading `alg` from anywhere else would be reading a field the object may not carry.

WHAT THE VERIFIER DOES WITH IT IS NOT ONE RULE BUT TWO, AND THE SCHEMA CANNOT PICK. For a `hybrid` registry entry the name is a machine suite and CR-4 compares it against the bundle's registered floor by CONTAINMENT of primitives, never by rank. For a `webauthn` entry it is one of HM-4's two key types, CR-8 puts a human leg outside that floor entirely, and HM-3 requires it to EQUAL the registry entry's `alg`, refusing a mismatch before a byte of the assertion is examined. Which rule applies is decided by the registry, which this object does not name, so the shape layer admits both vocabularies and narrows nothing. See `attestation_alg` below for why that is a union of two declarations and not a third list.

ADDED IN v1.3.31 (ACP-299), AS A CORRECTION AND NOT A FEATURE. This schema had no `alg` property through v1.3.30 while CR-5 called it an AT-1 field, `reference/src/acp_executor.py` listed it in `AT1_FIELDS` and `crates/acp-decision/src/quorum.rs` listed it in `AT1_FIELDS` and re-parsed it to pick the suite. The field set is CLOSED in both directions (AT-8b), so an object built from this file was refused by both verifiers for missing a field, and an object either verifier accepted carried a field this file called additional. The cross-language differential could not see it, because the two implementations agreed with each other and disagreed with the document -- the eighth lesson in `dossier/05-TEST-EVIDENCE.md`, and exactly the shape ACP-167 had one field over. `tools/check-attestation-object.py` is the executable consumer that would have caught it and now does.

proposal_hash.description: The canonical Proposal this attester signed. The binding the whole object exists to carry: the Executor verifies the executed proposal hashes to this value (9.3-3) rather than trusting that it does.

policy_bundle_hash.description: The signed bundle in force when the attestation was raised.

bundle_epoch.description: Epoch of that bundle. Monotonicity is enforced at the KMS against a durable high-water mark (RAD-3), never from this value.

context_snapshot_hash.description: The Context read the Decision was computed over (§8.8 `snapshot_hash()`).

floor_only_risk.description: FLOOR-ONLY risk, not effective risk. AT-3 requires the attester to have been shown floor tiers and the bundle `rule_id`s that raised the risk, NOT Context-asserted values — that separation is what closes A-8's display path. The Executor recomputes this from the signed bundle and the canonical Proposal (TR-8); a disagreement with the value here is a critical alert, because it means the signing substrate emitted a Decision the bundle does not support.

required_roles.description: Attester roles the rule demanded. `uniqueItems` because a repeated role is a second spelling of one requirement, and two spellings of one thing is the defect this repository is built around.

required_count.description:
The threshold the attester was shown and signed.

AT-9 places TWO requirements on this field and NEITHER SUBSTITUTES FOR THE OTHER. (1) It MUST NOT be an input to the quorum decision, in whole or in part, INCLUDING where every entry agrees on it: the threshold is taken from the signed bundle's `quorum_k` (PB-6) and is class R — recomputed. `required_count` is signed by the attester, and the attester is exactly the party under verification, so reading the threshold from it asks the adversary how large a quorum to demand. (2) It MUST nonetheless equal `quorum_k`, and a mismatch MUST fail closed with a critical alert — because it is part of what the attester was SHOWN (AT-3), so a mismatch means the humans approved under a policy the engine did not apply.

An implementation that keeps only (1) satisfies INV-1-HIGH while silently executing actions no attester agreed to. This clause exists because its absence was exploited — see the v1.3.15 alert in §1(a).

operator.description: The operator the action is attributed to. Carried HERE, inside the signature, so approver-distinctness (AT-2) and the §9.3 step-9 capability recheck key on a signature-covered value rather than a receipt-body claim. The receipt's top-level `operator` is diagnostic only. Mechanized as `Y4_OperatorTamperDetected`.

att_nonce.description: A fresh 128-bit attestation nonce (AT-1), making the derived `attestation_id` unique per attestation. Single use is enforced by ledger consumption of that id (AT-5, CL-3), not by assertion — v1.2.0 stated single-use as a property with no enforcing mechanism, which permitted attestation amplification (T-14).

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 instant, at most 60 minutes after issuance (AT-1). Expired attestations are void and partial quorum at expiry is void (AT-5). Evaluated against NTS-disciplined wall time within the L-20 skew allowance, never against a monotonic clock — leg F9.1 carries that dependency and DP-52 states the distinction.

attestation_alg.description:
What an Attestation Object may declare as its suite: a machine suite (`SuiteId`, the set CR-4's floor is registered in) or a human key type (`WebauthnAlg`, HM-4's two, which CR-8 puts outside that floor). The two are declared once each, in the SIGNED root, and pointed at from here.

WHY A UNION AND NOT A THIRD LIST. A single enum naming all five values is the obvious way to write this field and it is the defect this repository publishes corrections for. The names would then exist in three places: CR-4 compares an object's suite against `min_suite`, which is drawn from `signature.schema.json`, and HM-3 compares it against a `webauthn` registry entry's `alg`, which is drawn from `attesters.schema.json`. A comparison between a copy and its original passes on a vocabulary nobody checked -- `decision_receipt.alg` records the same argument for `SuiteId` alone, and CR-8's restriction is exactly what forbids the cheaper fix of widening `SuiteId` to five values: `webauthn-es256` and `webauthn-ed25519` MUST NOT appear as a bundle, receipt or door suite, and every other holder of `SuiteId` is one of those three positions.

WHY THE GENERATOR ACCEPTS IT. `tools/codegen.py` reads a `oneOf` as a union it must be able to DECIDE, and refuses one it would have to resolve by trying branches until something fits. A tagged union of objects proves its discriminator from the schema; this one is proved a different way and the proof is just as mechanical: the branches are named enums and the generator halts unless their value sets are pairwise DISJOINT, so exactly one branch can match any given string and the decode is by value rather than by order. Adding a value to either declaration that already exists in the other turns the generator red rather than emitting a type whose meaning depends on branch order.

BOTH BRANCHES CROSS ROOTS, AND ONLY A NAMED SCALAR MAY (ACP-78 M1). The signed side owns the vocabulary and the wire carries it, the same direction as `SuiteId`, `Tier` and `FidelityClass`. This type is nevertheless declared HERE rather than in the bundle root, because the union is a fact about a MESSAGE: no signed table holds a value that may be either, and a registry entry's `alg` is always exactly one of the two.

sha256.description: `"sha256:"` followed by a lowercase-hex SHA-256 digest — 71 characters. The type is pinned rather than left to the implementer because §11.2 records an implementer who fed forward raw digest bytes and built a different chain while following the text.

nonce128.description:
A 128-bit nonce: `"b64:"` followed by RFC 4648 §4 base64 WITH padding, carried, hashed and signed as that string (WE-4). The size is AT-1 for the attestation nonce and L-17 for the receipt nonce.

THE PATTERN IS TWO RULES, AND THEY REFUSE UNDER DIFFERENT NAMES. `b64:` plus the RFC 4648 §4 alphabet with padding is WE-4, the wire type; the twenty-four characters are the 128 bits. A verifier folding them into one check answers `WE-4` for a 64-bit nonce, which is a perfectly well-formed `b64:` value — the wrong clause name, and the cross-language differential compares names. `reference/src/acp_executor.py` and `crates/acp-decision/src/quorum.rs` both apply the type rule first and the size rule second, in that order, because an object wrong in both ways must stop at the same rule everywhere.

WHY THE PREFIX IS PART OF THE VALUE. `attestation_id` is SHA-256 over the canonical CBOR of the Attestation Object (AT-8a), so an issuer carrying `b64:AAAA…` and a verifier carrying `AAAA…` derive TWO IDS FOR ONE OBJECT and claim TWO LEDGER SLOTS — one human approval, spent twice. That is Z4 and T-14 reopening through a type nobody had written down, reached with no optional field and therefore untouched by AT-8b, which closes the field set one layer above this. §11.2 pins `sha256:` to the character for the same reason and records what happened without it: an implementer who fed forward raw digest bytes built a different chain while following the text.

HISTORY, KEPT BECAUSE IT IS THE ARGUMENT. When this schema was first written the prefix was pinned HERE and nowhere else — `b64:` occurred exactly twice in ZIFFER-SPEC-001, both times inside §9.2's diagnostic JSON, and no clause said whether it was part of the value. Writing the schema is what surfaced that (ACP-87); it is now fixed at the root as WE-4 in v1.3.18, so this pattern restates the specification rather than exceeding it. A type that exists only in a schema is a type the specification does not have, and a second implementation written from the document alone would never have seen it.

The three definitions of this type — here, the Python reference and the Rust verifier — DID diverge, and no gate noticed: this pattern pinned twenty-four characters from its first day while the reference accepted any length, and no fixture ever fed a wrong-length nonce. `tools/nonce-type-vectors.json` is now the one corpus all three are evaluated against, and `tools/check-nonce-type.py` resolves this `$def` rather than one field's inline pattern, so the corpus is evaluated against the type every nonce field shares.

IT IS ONE TYPE AND IT LIVES HERE. ACP-78 M1 found FIVE definitions of it inside `spec/schemas/wire/` alone — an inline pattern on this object's `att_nonce` and on `PendingRelease.receipt_nonce`, and named copies in the audit record and the ledger claim — with the sentence above, saying the definitions must move together, sitting inside two of them. `$ref` it; do not restate it.

operator_id.description:
A party identity: the operator an action is attributed to, and the same value DR-9 compares an acknowledger against.

NO CLAUSE TYPES THIS AND THAT IS THE POINT OF SAYING SO HERE. ZIFFER-SPEC-001 carries `operator`, attester identities and notification recipients as bare strings everywhere and states no syntax, no length and no namespace for any of them. The bound is DERIVED, not restated: an operator must resolve in the bundle's attester registry for AT-2 approver-distinctness and DR-9 to be decidable, and `spec/schemas/bundle/attesters.schema.json` bounds that registry's keys at 1..128 — itself a schema-level choice with no clause behind it. So this is a schema constraint the specification does not make, in the ACP-87 shape: a type that exists only in a schema is a type the specification does not have.

IT IS DECLARED ONCE BECAUSE IT WAS DECLARED FIVE TIMES. ACP-78 M1 found this value written inline in five places across this root with TWO different bounds — 128 here, in `ContextRead.capability_grant`, in the receipt and in the pending-release record, and 2,048 in the audit record, where its author derived the bound from L-04 instead. Two lengths for one identity means a party who is nameable in an audit record and unnameable in the receipt that produced it.

rfc3339_instant.description:
An instant on the wire: EXACTLY `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, to one second. No offset, no fractional part, no lowercase `z`. Every temporal value in this root carries this type except the acknowledgement's, which ACK-6 declares numeric.

WHY THE SPELLING IS PINNED AND NOT LEFT TO RFC 3339 AS WRITTEN. RFC 3339 accepts `2026-08-09T14:02:11Z`, `2026-08-09t14:02:11z`, `2026-08-09T16:02:11+02:00` and `2026-08-09T14:02:11.000Z` as four renderings of ONE instant. Each is a distinct string, and these values go inside canonical CBOR and are hashed: the receipt's `issued_at` sits in the signed body, the attestation object's `expires_at` sits in the preimage of `attestation_id` (AT-1, AT-8a), and `occurred_at` sits in the AU-1 chain preimage. Four spellings of one instant are four ids for one object and four chain hashes for one history -- Z4 and T-14 reopening through a type nobody had written down, which is precisely what `nonce128` above records happening to `b64:`. Canonicalization cannot fix it: the ambiguity is in the VALUE, not the encoding. So the offset MUST be `Z`, the letters MUST be upper case, there MUST be no fractional part, and a verifier MUST REJECT any other rendering rather than normalizing it -- normalizing here would make this verifier accept every spelling and hand the divergence to the next implementation, which is the reasoning `nonce128` gives for refusing a stripped `b64:` prefix.

WHY IT IS A STRING AND NOT AN EPOCH NUMBER. AT-8a forbids a float in a canonical structure because a float is not deterministically encoded, and `canon()` enforces that at the TOP level only -- a nested float serialises happily in both languages. The one structure in this root whose times are numbers is the acknowledgement, and the reference put `1787598182.1470501` into it on every production path (`crates/acp-core/src/generated_wire.rs` records the observation beside `AcknowledgementObject.issued_at`). A string of this shape has exactly one encoding.

HISTORY, KEPT BECAUSE IT IS THE ARGUMENT. Through v1.3.27 this type was written out on `audit_record.occurred_at` and NOWHERE ELSE; the other six temporal fields carried a bare `{"type": "string", "format": "date-time"}` with no pinned spelling, and BOTH implementations read all seven as POSIX numbers. So an Attestation Object that satisfied the schema was refused at `9.3-7b-iii` by both verifiers, and an object both verifiers accepted did not validate -- no client building from the schema could satisfy a floor-HIGH quorum. The cross-language differential could not see it, because the two implementations agreed with each other and disagreed with the document: the eighth lesson in `dossier/05-TEST-EVIDENCE.md`, one artifact over. Nothing validates a fixture against these schemas (ACP-52), so nothing else could either. Filed as ACP-167 by the first executable consumer to build a floor-HIGH fixture from the schema rather than from the reference, and closed in v1.3.28 by moving the IMPLEMENTATIONS -- because AT-1, section 9.2's rendered receipt and seven schemas all said RFC 3339, and only the code said otherwise. `anchor.schema.json` had already written the fix down: "a divergence to close in one place, not two".

THE PARSER ALREADY EXISTED, ONE ROOT OVER, AND THIS TYPE IS ITS GRAMMAR WRITTEN DOWN. PB-1 has to decide when a bundle stops being valid, so `bundle/manifest.schema.json` carries `expires_at` as RFC 3339 and both implementations parse it strictly: `Timestamp::parse` in Rust and `Timestamp.parse` in the reference, refusing offsets, fractional seconds and lowercase `z` in the same words, checking the day against the actual length of the month, and refusing a leap second because `datetime` does. They are already differential partners. This $def is that grammar, so the wire root gets ONE more reference to an existing type rather than a second parser -- a second parser for one format being the two-definitions defect this repository has published three corrections for. THE FRACTIONAL PART IS WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS HERE: `occurred_at`'s pattern through v1.3.27 permitted `(\.\d{1,9})?`, so `...:11Z` and `...:11.0Z` were two spellings of one instant inside the AU-1 chain preimage -- the exact hazard four paragraphs up, in the one field that had a pattern at all. v1.3.28 narrows it to the parsers' grammar. Nothing emitted a fractional second, because both implementations were emitting numbers.

IT IS ONE TYPE AND IT LIVES HERE, for the reason `nonce128` states one $def above.
